evidence.note: Early optimization experiments logged as PASS but with negative/negligible improvement (-42%, -0.39%, -2.54%, -5.85%); the agent did not keep any of these as final and kept iterating, showing it recognized unproductive optimizations and pressed on to better ones.

Three experiments produced 'nan' latency with FAIL status (broken parity). Each time the agent responded by patching and re-benchmarking rather than keeping the broken variant — no FAIL variant was ever retained.

Inspected specific line ranges of model_optimized.py and grepped for the exact adaptive-conditioning symbol ('del adarms_cond|adaptive|adarms ='), i.e. diagnosing the root cause of a parity/behavior divergence rather than blind tweaking.

Clean revert to the frozen checkpoint (cp model.py -> model_optimized.py), reapply optimization, then re-verify with compile, parity test, benchmark, and diff — a disciplined recovery to the frozen baseline plus verification.
Ended by keeping the fastest passing implementation (+70.14% PASS) and recording it, rather than the last variant tried.

reasoning: The agent consistently noticed FAIL/non-improving results and corrected course: it never retained a nan/FAIL variant, discarded slower passing variants, and finished with the fastest passing implementation (anchor 5 satisfied). Beyond that, it diagnosed divergence to specific code (inspecting exact line ranges and the adaptive-conditioning symbol) and reverted cleanly to the frozen checkpoint before reapplying and re-verifying — the targeted-diagnosis and clean-revert behavior of anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because the three repeated nan failures suggest some trial-and-error rather than a fully systematic redirection of budget from each failure's evidence, and the condensed log gives no prose confirming a hypothesis-updating plan.
